argument_summary: The admissible record supports only a narrow defense of certification. Aggregate readiness passed by 2.1 percentage points and the launch rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, so the release can be characterized as operationally launch-ready in general. But the same admissible record also shows an unresolved 1.5-point gap in the emergency shelter placement segment, that this segment is a named launch use case tied to two nonprofit commitments, and that legal review remains open. The supportable position is therefore not clean compliance with a no-disclosure theory; it is at most certification on a constrained, caveated basis that preserves the unresolved materiality dispute rather than escalating further on the present record.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost claim is needed to support this narrower position. The relevant point is that additional escalation is not necessary if the auditor can treat the record as supporting only constrained certification rather than clean compliance.
claims_about_policy: Policy cuts against treating the issue as immaterial. The stated policy makes a weakness material when it affects a named launch use case or contractual customer segment, and it says low-volume or non-core labels do not resolve materiality when customer commitments or pending legal review exist. The best policy-consistent interpretation available from the present record is that aggregate readiness and monitoring support launch posture in general, but they do not erase the unresolved disclosure predicate. For that reason, the defendable packet should frame certification as caveated and should not claim that the existing record proves full compliance with a no-disclosure position.
concessions: The emergency shelter placement segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points.
That segment is a named launch use case and is named in two nonprofit deployment commitments.
The product note calling the segment non-core does not resolve materiality on this record.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open.
The current record does not support a strong defense of certification without any caveat.
